AGENDA
  GLENDALE ARTS AND CULTURE COMMISSION
  COUNCIL CHAMBER, City Hall – 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
Welcome to Glendale City Hall. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast
throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for
purchase in the City Clerk’s Office. Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at
http://www.glendaleca.gov/government/agendas-minutes. If you have any question about matters on the
agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business
hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign language
translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices are available same-day
upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for requests regarding sign language
translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that
are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the
Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who wish to utilize
the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City Clerk’s office at 818-548-
2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify the language for which you require
translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their
own interpreter or speak in their native language.

  APRIL 18, 2019
  1. ROLL CALL
  a. Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the April 18, 2019
  Regular Meeting was Posted on April 15, 2019 on the Bulletin Board Outside City
  Hall.
  2. CONSENT ITEMS (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
  Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.
  a. Minutes of the Regular Arts and Culture Commission Meeting of March 21, 2019
  3. INTRODUCTIONS & PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Chuck Wike, Community Relations
  Manager.

  4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5
  Minutes. Members of the Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the
  Speaker, but there will be no Debate or Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff
  Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report.
 5. BUSINESS AGENDA
  A. ACTION ITEM(s)
  a. Motion allocating $3,100 from the Arts and Culture Commission 2019-2020 Work Plan
  to enable artist Scott Froschauer to redeploy, or fabricate, and install up to five signs
  from his Art Happens Anywhere “Word on the Street” program; and recommending that
  the Director of Library, Arts & Culture enter into an Art Display Agreement, in an
  amount not to exceed $3,100 in total, with Scott Froschauer to redeploy, or fabricate,
  and install the signs in locations subject to City departments’ approval, for a fixed
  period of time that the Commission determines.
  b. Nominations for Artist Selection Committees
  i. Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station
  ii. Brand Library Summer Plaza Series
  iii. Beyond the Box Utility Box Mural Program

  B. DISCUSSION ITEM(s)
  a. 2019-2020 Work Plan Progress
  i.  CITY-WIDE ARTS
  a. Beyond The Box Utility Box Murals
  ii.  NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS
  a. Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station
  iii.  PERFORMING ARTS
  a. Brand Plaza and 222 EAST Performance Series
  iv.  ARTS & CULTURAL EVENTS
  a. Art Walk
  v.  Staffing Actions

  b. Culver City Art in Public Places Visit
  c. Future designation of art as temporary or permanent

6. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
7. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS
8. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission is May 16, 2019, at 2:00 p.m.
  in the City Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor.
minutes_text:
CITY OF GLENDALE
  ARTS and CULTURE COMMISSION
  Minutes of Regular Meeting

  Thursday, April 18, 2019 at 2:00 p.m.
1. ROLL CALL
  • The meeting was called to order on April 18, 2019 at 2:03 p.m.
  • Present: Commissioners Oshagan, Tufenkian, Vice Chair Zadorian, Chairperson Vidor

2. REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA
  A. Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the April 18, 2019 Regular Meeting was
  Posted on Friday, April 15, 2019 on the Bulletin Board Outside City Half.

3. CONSENT ITEMS (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  A  Approval of Regular Meeting Minutes from March 21, 2019

  Moved:  Commissioner Oshagan
  Seconded:  Vice Chair Zadorian
  A roll call was conducted and the Commissioners voted as follows:
  Ayes:  Commissioners Oshagan, Tufenkian, Vice Chair Zadorian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

4. INTRODUCTIONS & PRESENTATIONS
  A Library, Arts & Culture Events - Presented by Chuck Wike, Community Relations Manager
  • Mr. Wike gave an overview of current and upcoming events at Glendale Library, Arts & Culture locations.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Speaker{s):
  1. Cathy Hrenda of Adams Hill Neighborhood Association spoke about Adams Hill Mini Park Gas Station Artist
  call and requested that improvements be made to the City web site.
  2. Taryn Newton-Gill of FOUND Arts Agency spoke about helping to provide artists for Glendale's 2019 Arts
  Initiatives via her company's services.
  3. Karl West of Swains HQ Art supply spoke about the Arts District, mentioned his company's new and
  expanded location, and requested consideration of the expansion of the Arts & Entertainment District to
  include his store.
  4. Armina LaManna of Imagine Project spoke about a new nonprofit children's theatre opening in Burbank.

6. BUSINESS AGENDA
  A. ACTION ITEM(s)
  Motion allocating $8,000 from the Arts and Culture Commission 2019-2020 Work Plan to enable artist Scott
  Froschauer to redeploy, or fabricate, and install up to eighteen signs from his Art Happens Anywhere 'Word
  on the Street" program; and recommending that the Director of Library, Arts & Culture enter into an Art
  Display Agreement, in an amount not to exceed $8,000 plus up to $2,000 for maintenance in total, with Scott
  Froschauer to redeploy, or fabricate, and install the signs in locations subject to City departments' approval,
  for up to two years.

  Moved: Commissioner Oshagan
   Seconded:  Vice Chair Zadorian
  A roll call was conducted and the Commissioners voted as follows:
  Ayes:  Commissioners Oshagan, Tufenkian, Vice Chair Zadorian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

  a. Nominations for Artist Selection Committees
  i. Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station
  ii. Brand Library Summer Plaza Series
  iii. Beyond the Box Utility Box Mural Program

  Motion to accept nominations for Commissioners Sevana Zadorian and CarolineTufenkian on
  the Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station committee; Commissioners Arlene Vidor and
  CarolineTufenkian on the Brand Library Summer Plaza Series committee; Commissioners Ara
  Oshagan and Sevana Zadorian on the Beyond the Box Utility Box Mural Program committee.

  Moved:  Vice Chair Zadorian
  Seconded:  Commissioner Tufenkian
  A roll call was conducted and the Commissioners voted as follows:
  Ayes:  Commissioners Oshagan, Tufenkian, Vice Chair Zadorian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

B. DISCUSSION ITEM{s)
  a. 2019-2020 Work Plan Progress
  • Mr. Wike provided a brief update on the Work Plan progress and programs that have had recent
  activity.
  • At the end of the City Wide Arts discussion regarding Beyond the Box Utility Box Mural Program,
  Chair Vidor requested that staff bring back a future discussion about the opportunity to wrap
  boxes rather than paint them and also rotating box paintings.
  • At the end of the Neighborhood Arts discussion regarding Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station,
  Chair Vidor requested that staff place an action item regarding CaFE, a leading website for
  managing call for entries, program on next month's agenda.
  • After Mr. Wike updated the Commission on Performing Arts, Blair Whittington, Music Specialist at
  Brand Library gave the Commission some highlights of the upcoming Brand Plaza Summer
  Series.
  • The Commission asked questions, and gave their thoughts and feedback on other specific
  programs under the Work Plan.

  b. Culver City Art in Public Places Visit
  • Chair Vidor and Director Shaffer gave a brief summary about the findings and materials from the
  trip they took to visit staff at the City of Culver City who manage the city's art program.
  c. Future designation of art as temporary or permanent
  • Director Shaffer provided definitions and examples of temporary and permanent art. He also
  spoke about the maintenance of permanent art pieces. He stated that this item is a discussion
  item and there will be no action taken at this time.

  2
 7. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
  • Commissioner Zadorian:
  • Thanked the Beyond the Box Utility Box Mural program artists for sharing their talent with
  Glendale;
  •  Announced an upcoming event called Glendale Out, an LGBTQ art exhibition displayed at
  Crescenta Valley High school from May 14th_ 17th; opening day is on Monday, May 13
  from 3:30 pm to 6:00 pm; and
  •  Stated the Glendale Out art exhibition will be displayed sometime in June at Roslyn
  Gallery or Ace 21 Gallery. She will have more information at next month's meeting.
  • Commissioner Oshagan:
  •  Along with Chair Vidor, requested staff to bring back a report that better defines the
  definition of "temporary art"; and
  •  Asked staff to clarify if the selection committee for the Brand Plaza Series would also
  select for 222 East performance series. Mr. Wike stated that one committee will select for
  both programs.
  • Chair Vidor requested that staff place the following items on future agendas:
  •  An Action item for a downtown ART WALK, that might include up to two gallery spaces on
  Artsakh Plaza if the City would be willing and able to grant access to the spaces for the
  ART WALK;
  •  Website enhancements to calls that we can make to the existing site; clarify all calls on
  A&C Commission site and hyperlink to calls, incorporate photos where possible and
  collect more photos, also look into posting all calls on CaFE;
  •  A discussion on including non-commissioner/city staff members on selection committees;
  and
  •  A discussion on murals and how the Commission can go about supporting requests for
  murals.

8. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS - None
9. ADJOURNMENT - 3:56 p.m.

  The next regular meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission is May 16, 2019, at 2:00 p.m. in the City Council
  Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor.
